questions.q: A particle goes from $\text{A}$ to $\text{B}$ with a speed of $\text{40 km/h}$ and $\text{B}$ to $\text{C}$ with a speed of $\text{60 km/h}$. If $\text{AB} = 6\text{BC}$, the average speed in $\text{km/h}$ between $\text{A}$ and $\text{C}$ is
questions.solution:
${\text{V}}_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{\text{distance travelled}}{\text{time taken}}$

$⇒ {\text{V}}_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{\text{AB} + \text{BC}}{\dfrac{\text{AB}}{4 0} + \dfrac{\text{BC}}{6 0}}$

${⇒ \text{V}}_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{\text{6BC} + \text{BC}}{\dfrac{\text{6BC}}{4 0} + \dfrac{\text{BC}}{6 0}}$

${\text{V}}_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{7 \times 2 4 0}{3 6 + 4} ⇒ {\text{V}}_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{7 \times 2 4 0}{4 0}$

$⇒ {\text{V}}_{\text{av}} = 4 2 \text{km/h}$

questions.q: Two trains $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ of length $\text{400 m}$ each are moving on two parallel tracks with a uniform speed of $72\dfrac{km}{h}$ in the same direction, with $\text{A}$ ahead of $\text{B}$. The driver of $\text{B}$ decides to overtake $\text{A}$ and accelerates by $1\dfrac{m}{s2}$. If after $\text{50 s}$, the guard of $\text{B}$ just brushes past the driver of $\text{A}$~and the original distance between them is $x$, then calculate value of $\dfrac{x}{10}$ ?
questions.solution:
Length of each train,

${l ⁡}_{A} = {l ⁡}_{B} = 4 0 0 \text{m}$

$u{⁡}_{A ⁡} = 72 \times \dfrac{5}{18}\text{m/s}$

$\text{= 20 m/s}$

Distance travelled by train $\text{A}$ in $\text{50 s}$

${s}_{A} = {u}_{A} \times \text{t}$

(As for unaccelerated motion, distance = Speed x Time)

${s}_{A} = 2 0 \times 5 0$

$\text{= 1000 m}$

Distance travelled by train $\text{B}$ in $\text{50 s}$,

${s}_{B} = {u}_{B} \text{t} + \dfrac{1}{2} {a}_{B} t^{2}$

(As motion of train B is an accelerated motion)

${s}_{B} = 2 0 \times 5 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times {\left(5 0\right)}^{2}$

$\text{= 1000 + 1250}$

$\text{= 2250 m}$

relative distance between the two trains ${\text{=S}}_{B} - {S}_{A}$

$\text{= 2250 - 1000}$

$\text{= 1250 m}$
we should subtract~$2l$ from it where $l$~is length of train so final answer will be 450 m

Alternate Method

Initially, both the trains are moving with same speed, the train $\text{B}$ first comes that of the train $\text{A}$ in $\text{50 s}$ with an acceleration of $\text{50 s}$.

$∴$ Original distance between the trains

= Distance covered by train $\text{B}$ with an acceleration a

$= \text{ut} + \dfrac{1}{2} {at}^{2}$

$= 0 \times 5 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times {\left(5 0\right)}^{2}$

(As both train starts with same velocity, so velocity, so velocity of train when it starts accelerating can be taken as zero).

$\text{= 1250 m}$ .

we should subtract $2l$ from it where $l$ is length of train so final answer will be $\text{450 m}$

questions.q: A particle undergoes a one-dimensional motion such that its velocity varies according to $v\left(x\right) = \betax^{- 2n}$, where $\beta$ and $\text{n}$ are constants and $\text{x}$ is the position of the particle. The acceleration of the particle as a function of $\text{x}$& is given by
questions.solution:
According to the question

$a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v \left(\dfrac{d}{dx}\betax^{-2n}\right)

$= $\left(-2n\betax^{-2n - 1}\right)\betax^{- 2n}$

$= - 2n{\beta$}^{2}x^{- 4n - 1}

questions.q: A point moves in the $x - y$ plane according to $x = Asin\omegat$ and $y = A  \left(1 – \text\cos\omegat\right)$ where $A$ and \omega are positive constants. The distance traversed by the point during the time $τ& is$
questions.solution:
Distance travelled by point in time t is:
$S = {∫}_{0}^{τ}\left|\overset{→}{V}\right|dt$
$∵ \left|\overset{→}{V}\right| = \sqrt{{{V}_{x}}^{2} + {{V}_{y}}^{2}}$
Where, ${V}_{x} = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = A\omegacos ⁡ \omegat and{V}_{y} = \dfrac{dy}{dt} = A\omegasin ⁡ \omegat$
$S = {∫}_{0}^{τ}A\omegadt = A\omegaτ$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two objects $P$ and $Q$, travelling in the same direction start from rest. While the object $P$ starts at time $t = 0$ and object $Q$ starts later at $t = 30min$. The object $P$ has an acceleration of $40km / h^{2}$. To catch $P$ at a distance of $20$ km, the acceleration of $Q$ should be
questions.solution:
According to question,

Object $P$ starts at $t = 0$ and acceleration of $P = 40km / h^{2}$

The time taken by object $P$ to cover $20$ km will be,

$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}$

Where, $u = 0, s = \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}$

$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{a}}$

Here, $a = 40km / h^{2}$

and $s = 20km$

$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 20}{40}}$

$= 1hour$

Time taken by $Q$ will be $\dfrac{1}{2}hour$, because it started after $30min$.

The acceleration in $Q$,

$a = \dfrac{2s}{t2} = \dfrac{2 \times 20}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2}$

$= 2 \times 4 \times 20$

$= 160km / h^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car moving with a speed of $50km{h}^{- 1}$ can be stopped by brakes in at least $6m$. If the same car is moving at a speed of $100km{h}^{- 1}$, then the minimum stopping distance (in $m$) is
questions.solution:
The stopping distance of a car is

$s = \dfrac{{u}^{2}}{2a}$

Therefore, for the two situations given in the question, we can write

$\dfrac{{s}_{1}}{{s}_{2}} = {\left(\dfrac{{u}_{1}}{{u}_{2}}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$\dfrac{6}{{s}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ {s}_{2} = 24m$

$a = \sqrt{{a}_x^{2} + {a}_y^{2}}$

$= \left[{\left(\dfrac{d^{2} \text{x}}{{dt}^{2}}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{d^{2} \text{y}}{{dt}^{2}}\right)}^{2}\right] \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car accelerates from rest at a constant rate of $2ms^{- 2}$ for some time. Then, it retards at a constant rate of $4ms^{- 2}$ and comes to rest. If the total time for which it remains in motion is $3s$, Then the total distance travelled is
questions.solution:
Using $v = u + atorv - u = at,$ we find that if $\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$ is doubled,~$t$~will be halved.

If& $t$ is the time for accelerations, then $\dfrac{t}{2}$ is the time for retardation.

Now, $t + \dfrac{t}{2} = 3$

or~$\dfrac{3t}{2} = 3$

$t = 2s$

$S = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 1 \times 1 = \left(4 + 2\right)m = 6m$

questions.q: A bullet emerges from a barrel of length $1. 2m$ with a speed of $640ms^{- 1}$. Assuming constant acceleration, the approximate time that is spent in the barrel after the gun is fired is
questions.solution:
Given, $s = 1.2m, v = 640\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}, a = ? , u = 0; t = ?$

We have the third equation of motion

$2as = v^{2} - u^{2}$

$2a \times 1.2 = 640 \times 640$

Or $a = \dfrac{8 \times 64 \times {10}^{3}}{3}$

And by first equation of motion

$v = u + at$

Or $t = \dfrac{v}{a} = \dfrac{15}{4} \times {10}^{- 3}$

$= 3.75 \times {10}^{- 3}s \approx 4ms$

questions.q: A target is made of two plates, one of wood and the other of iron. The thickness of the wooden plate is $4$ cm and that of the iron plate is $2$ cm. A bullet fired goes through the wood first and then penetrates $1$ cm into iron. A similar bullet fired with the same velocity from the opposite direction goes through iron first and then penetrates $2$ cm into the wood. If ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ be the retardation offered to the bullet by wood and iron plates respectively, then
questions.solution:
Let ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ be the retardations offered to be bullet by wood and iron respectively.

For $A \to B \to C,$

${v}_{1}^{2} - u^{2} = 2{a}_{1}\left(4\right),$ and ${0}^{2} - {v}_{1}^{2} = 2{a}_{2} ( 1 )$

Adding, we get

$- u^{2} = 2 ( 4{a}_{1} + {a}_{2} )$...(i)

For $A^{′} \to B^{′} \to C^{′},$

${v}_{2}^{2} - u^{2} = 2{a}_{2} \left(2\right)$

and ${0}^{2} - {v}_{2}^{2} = 2{a}_{1} \left(2\right)$

Adding, we get

$- u^{2} = 2 ( 2{a}_{1} + 2{a}_{2} )$....(ii)

Equating Eqs. (i) and (ii) and solving, we get

$4{a}_{1} + {a}_{2} = 2{a}_{1} + 2{a}_{2}$

$⇒ {a}_{2} = 2{a}_{1}$

Let the man starts crossing the road at an angle θ shown in figure. For safe crossing the condition is that the man must cross the road by the time the truck describes the distance 4 + AC or 4 + 2 cot θ.

or & & & & & & & & & 2 cos θ - sin θ = 0

${v}_\min = \dfrac{8}{\text{2} ( \dfrac{2}{5} ) + \dfrac{1}{5}} = \dfrac{8}{5}ms^{- 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle starts from rest and traverses a distance $2x$ with uniform acceleration, then moves uniformly over a further distance $4x$ and finally comes to rest after moving a further distance $6x$ under uniform retardation. Assuming entire motion to be rectilinear motion, the ratio of average speed over the journey to the maximum speed on its way is
questions.solution:
Let ${t}_{1}$,${t}_{2}$ and ${t}_{3}$ be the time taken by the particles to cover the distance $2x$, $4x$ and $6x$ respectively. Let $v$ be the velocity of the particle at $B$ i.e, maximum velocity. The particle moves with uniform acceleration from $A$ to $B$.

For motion from $A$ to $B$.

Average velocity $= \dfrac{0 + v}{2} = \dfrac{v}{2}$

Time taken, ${t}_{1} = \dfrac{2x}{\dfrac{v}{2}}$

Particle moves with uniform retardation from $C$ TO $D$, ${V}_{avg} = \dfrac{0 + v}{2} = \dfrac{v}{2}$

Time taken ,${t}_{3} = \dfrac{6x}{( \dfrac{v}{2} )}$

Total time = ${t}_{1} + {t}_{2} + {t}_{3}$

$t = \dfrac{2x}{v2} + \dfrac{4x}{v} + \dfrac{6x}{v2} = \dfrac{20x}{v}$

Average Velocity over= $\dfrac{6x + 2x + 4x}{20xv} = \dfrac{3}{5}v$
Required Ratio =& $\dfrac{Average Speed}{v} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

questions.q: A boat covers $24km$ upstream and $36km$ downstream in $6hours$ while it covers $36km$ upstream and $24km$ downstream in $6\dfrac{1}{2}$ $hours$. The velocity (in $kmph$) of the current is
questions.solution:
Let rate of upstream = x kmph and rate of downstream = y kmph.

Then, $\dfrac{24}{x} + \dfrac{36}{y} = 6 \ldots . ( i )$ and $\dfrac{36}{x} + \dfrac{24}{y} = \dfrac{13}{2} \ldots . ( ii )$

Solving (i) & (ii) $y = 12km{hr}^{- 1}$ and $x = 8km{hr}^{- 1}$

$∴$Speed upstream = 8 kmph, Speed downstream = 12 kmph.

Hence, rate of current $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(12 - 8\right)$ kmph = $2kmph$.

questions.solution:
Velocity along $x$ direction is

${v}_{x} = {v}_{0 2} + \text{at}$

${v}_{x} = 3 + \left(- 1\right) t$

so when particle reach maximum $x$ coordinate ${v}_{x} = 0 ⇒ t = 3 sec$

similarly ${v}_{y} = {v}_{0 y} + {a}_{y} t$

questions.q: A wooden block of mass $10gm$ is dropped from the top of a tower $100m$ high. Simultaneously, a bullet of mass $10gm$ is fired from the foot of the tower vertically upwards with a velocity of $100m{s}^{- 1}$ . If the bullet is embedded in it, how high will it rise above the tower before it starts falling? $\left(g = 10m{s}^{- 2}\right)$
questions.solution:
Block and bullet will collide after $1s$ at height $95m$ from ground.

$Velocityofblockbeforecollision = gt = 10m{s}^{- 1}$

$Velocityofbulletbeforecollision = u – gt = 90m{s}^{- 1}$

from conservation of linear momentum,

$m\left(– 10\right) + m\left(90\right) = 2mv′ ⇒ v′ = 40m{s}^{- 1}$




Thus height raised by the combined mass

$h = \dfrac{v{′}^{2}}{2g} = \dfrac{40 \times 40}{2 \times 10} = 80m$

$heightfromtower = 75m$

questions.q: Two stations A and B are 110 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 7 a.m. and travels towards B at 20 kmph. Another train starts from B at 8 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 25 kmph. How many hours after the start, the train which starts from station A, will meet the other train which is coming from station B?
questions.solution:
Suppose they meet $x$ hours after 7 a.m.

Distance covered by A in $x$ hours = 20$x$ km.

Distance covered by B in $( x – 1 )$ hours $= 25 ( x – 1 ) km$

$20x + 25 ( x - 1 ) = 110$

$45x = 135 ⇒ x = 3 hr$

questions.q: A particle moves according to the law $x = rcos ⁡ \dfrac{\pit}{2}$. The distance covered by it in the time interval between $t = 0$ and $t = 3s$ is $nr$. What is the value of $n$?
questions.solution:
Given, $x = rcos ⁡ \dfrac{\pit}{2}$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$= - \dfrac{\pi}{2}rsin ⁡ \dfrac{\pit}{2}$

Graphically it can be represented as shown in figure.



Distance covered by the particle

$=$ Magnitude of area of $x - t$ curve between

$0$ to $2 s$ and $2$ to $3 s$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}vdt + {∫}_{2}^{3}vdt$

$= \left|- {∫}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{2}rsin ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{2}tdt\right| + \left|{∫}_{2}^{3}- \dfrac{\pi}{2}rsin ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{2}tdt\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{- \pi}{2}r{∫}_{0}^{2}sin ⁡ \dfrac{\pit}{2}dt\right| + \left|\dfrac{- \pi}{2}r{∫}_{2}^{3}sin ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{2}tdt\right|$

$= \left|{\left[\dfrac{\pir}{2}\dfrac{cos ⁡ \dfrac{\pit}{2}}{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\right]}_{0}^{2}\right| + \left|{\left[\dfrac{\pir}{2}\dfrac{cos ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{2}t}{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\right]}_{2}^{3}\right|$

$= \left|r\left(cos ⁡ \pi - cos ⁡ 0\right)\right| + \left|r\left(cos ⁡ \dfrac{3\pi}{2} - cos ⁡ \pi\right)\right|$

$= r\left|- 1 - 1\right| + r\left|0 - \left(- 1\right)\right| = 2r + r = 3r$

questions.solution:
Equation of motion is $y = β x^{2}$

$\dfrac{d^{2} y}{{dt}^{2}} = α$

$\dfrac{d^{2} x}{{dt}^{2}} = 0$

from $y = x$

$\dfrac{\text{dy}}{\text{dt}} = 2 x \dfrac{dx}{\text{dt}} β$

$\dfrac{d^{2} y}{{dt}^{2}} = \left(2 {\left(\dfrac{\text{dx}}{\text{dt}}\right)}^{2} + \text{2x} \dfrac{d^{2} x}{{dt}^{2}}\right) β$

${a}_{y} = \left(2 {\left(\dfrac{\text{dx}}{\text{dt}}\right)}^{2} + 0\right) β$

${a}_{y} = 2 {v}_x^{2} β$

${v}_{x} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{a}_{y}}{2 β}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{α}{2 β}}$

From equation ${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2as$

Given, $u = 0, a = \dfrac{g}{8}$

$∴$ We have, $v = \sqrt{2\left(\dfrac{g}{8}\right)h}$

When the stone released from this balloon. It will go upward with velocity $v = \sqrt{gh}$

In this condition, time taken by stone to reach the ground,

$- h = vt - \dfrac{1}{2} g{t}^{2}$

$t = \dfrac{v}{g}\left[1 + \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{2gh}{{v}^{2}}}\right]$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{\sqrt{gh}}{2}}{g}\left[1 + \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{2gh}{\dfrac{gh}{4}}}\right]$

$= \dfrac{2\sqrt{gh}}{g} = 2\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}}$

${S}_{2} = {v}_{1}\text{t} + \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}⇒ {v}_{0}t + \dfrac{3}{2}at^{2}$

${v}_{2} = {v}_{1} + \text{at}$

$= {v}_{0} + 2\text{at}$

${S}_{3} = {v}_{2}\text{t} + \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}$

$= {v}_{0}\text{t} + \dfrac{5}{2}{at}^{2}$

${v}_{0} = 0$

${S}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}$; ${S}_{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}{at}^{2}$; ${S}_{3} = \dfrac{5}{2}{at}^{2}$

${S}_{1}\text{:}{S}_{2}\text{:}{S}_{3} = \text{1}\text{:}3\text{:}5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A train of length $L$ move with a constant speed ${V}_{t}.$ A person at the back of the train fires a bullet at time $t = 0$ towards a target which is at a distance of $D$ (at time $t = 0$ ) from the front of the train (on the same direction of motion). Another person at the front of the train fires another bullet at time $t = T$ towards the same target. Both bullets reach the target at the same time. Assuming the speed of the bullets ${V}_{b}$ are same, the length of the train is
questions.solution:
Bullets from both person reaches target at same instant, so we equate time to get,

$\dfrac{L + D}{( {v}_{t} + {v}_{b} )} = \dfrac{D}{( {v}_{b} + {v}_{t} )} + T$

$L = ( {v}_{b} + {v}_{t} )T$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration experienced by a moving boat after is engine is cut-off, is given by $a = - kv^{3},$ where $k$ is a constant. If ${v}_{0}$ is the magnitude of velocity at cut-off, then the magnitude of the velocity at time $t$ after the cut off is
questions.solution:
Given, acceleration $a = - kv^{3}$

Initial velocity at cut-off, ${v}_{1} = {v}_{0}$

Initial time of cut-off, $t = 0$

And final time after cut-off, ${t}_{2} = t$

Again, $a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = - kv^{3}$

Or $\dfrac{dv}{v^{3}} = - kdt$

Integrating both sides, with in the condition of motion.

${∫}_{{v}_{0}}^{v}\dfrac{dv}{v^{3}} = - {∫}_{0}^{t}kdt$

Or ${\left[- \dfrac{1}{2v^{2}}\right]}_{{v}_{0}}^{v} = - {\left[kt\right]}_{0}^{t}$

Or $\dfrac{1}{2v^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2{v}_{0}^{2}} = kt$

Or $v = \dfrac{{v}_{0}}{\sqrt{1 + 2kt{v}_{0}^{2}}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the top of a tower of height 50m, a ball is thrown vertically upwards with a certain velocity. It hits the ground 10 s after it is thrown up. How much time does it take to cover a distance $AB$ where $A$ and $B$ are two points 20m and 40m below the edge of the tower? (g = 10ms^{- 2}$)$
questions.solution:
Let the body be projected upwards with velocity $u$ from top of tower. Taking vertical downward motion of body form top of tower to ground, we have

$u = - u, a = g = 10ms^{- 2}, s = 50m, t = 10$ s

As $s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$,

So, $50 = - u \times 10 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times {10}^{2}$

On solving $u = 45ms^{- 1}$

If ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$ are the timings taken by the ball to reach points $A$ and $B$ respectively, then

$20 = 45{t}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times {t}_{1}^{2}$

and $40 = - 45{t}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times {t}_{2}^{2}$

On solving, we get ${t}_{1} = 9.4$ s and ${t}_{2} = 9.8$ s

Time taken to cover the distance $AB$

$= \left({t}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right) = 9.8 = 9.4 = 0.4$ s.
